papers.title: MOTIVATIONS, TRAINING OUTCOMES, AND CLINICAL PRACTICE CHARACTERISTICS OF NORTH AMERICAN CHIROPRACTORS: A CROSS-SECTIONAL SURVEY
papers.one_line: North American chiropractors report prosocial motivations, strong clinical reasoning and communication skills, with practice patterns aligned to subluxation beliefs.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors are primarily motivated by helping patients and finding meaning in practice rather than status or money. Focus on clinical reasoning, patient communication, and lifestyle counseling—areas where training outcomes are strongest—while implementing evidence-based imaging stewardship. Aligning recruitment and education with these purpose-driven motivations may improve both practitioner satisfaction and patient outcomes.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractors reported prosocial, meaning-oriented motivations; strongest training outcomes in clinical reasoning, communication, and counseling; and practice patterns (manipulation frequency, x-ray use) correlated with subluxation-based practice orientation rather than biomedical alignment.

papers.title: Profession-Related Accreditation Requirements in Australia Regarding Anatomy Teaching: A Web-Based Desktop Audit
papers.one_line: Most Australian health profession accreditation standards lack specific anatomy curriculum requirements.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should advocate for explicit anatomy competency standards in accreditation frameworks, as only 6 of 20 health disciplines have specific anatomy requirements. Current vague accreditation language may allow inadequate anatomy training despite its critical importance for safe manipulative practice. Chiropractic programs should proactively establish and document rigorous functional anatomy standards independent of accreditation minimums.
papers.key_finding: Only 6 of 20 Australian health professions had specific accreditation requirements for anatomy curriculum content, with chiropractic notably lacking explicit standards despite anatomy being foundational to practice.
papers.study_design: Web-based desktop audit with content analysis

papers.title: Pediatric vertebral artery dissection and ischemic stroke following chiropractic manipulation.
papers.one_line: Chiropractic cervical manipulation associated with vertebral artery dissection in toddler.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should exercise extreme caution with cervical manipulation in pediatric patients, as VAD risk exists even in very young children with non-specific presentations (lethargy, vomiting, respiratory distress). Thorough pre-treatment screening and awareness of dissection symptoms are essential; consider referral for imaging if suspicious signs emerge post-treatment.
papers.key_finding: A 20-month-old presented with acute lethargy, vomiting, cyanosis, and respiratory distress following cervical chiropractic manipulation; imaging confirmed right vertebral artery dissection in the V4 segment.

papers.title: Assessing the importance and feasibility of quality measures for chiropractic care: a national survey of U.S. chiropractors.
papers.one_line: National survey identifies chiropractors' views on importance and feasibility of quality measures.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This survey provides insight into which quality metrics chiropractors consider most important and feasible to implement in practice. Understanding practitioner perspectives on quality measures can inform development of profession-wide standards and benchmarks for care.
papers.key_finding: The study assessed U.S. chiropractors' opinions regarding the importance and implementation feasibility of quality measures for chiropractic care through national survey methodology.

papers.title: Estimating Lumbar Spine Foraminal Disc Measurements Using Ultrasound and X-Ray Imaging Through Advanced Image Annotation, Processing, and Mathematical Modeling During Chiropractic Traction Procedures: A Feasibility Study
papers.one_line: Combined ultrasound and X-ray imaging with mathematical modeling quantifies lumbar spine changes during traction.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This feasibility study demonstrates that integrated ultrasound and X-ray measurements can objectively document spinal elongation during traction procedures, potentially standardizing outcome assessment. Chiropractors could use these methods to quantify treatment response at specific spinal levels and grades of traction force, improving documentation and patient education regarding mechanical decompression.
papers.key_finding: Progressive traction forces (1.8–11.3 kg) produced consistent increases in lumbar spinal height and foraminal area across L3-L4, L4-L5, and L5-S1 levels; mathematical scaling factors successfully standardized measurements between X-ray and ultrasound modalities.

papers.title: Cervical spinal manipulative therapy, arterial dissection, and the law: Informed consent and causation in Goldie C.arsenault
papers.one_line: Canadian court found chiropractor liable for cervical artery dissection stroke despite uncertain causation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This case highlights the critical importance of comprehensive informed consent documentation for cervical manipulation, particularly regarding arterial dissection risk. Chiropractors should ensure consent forms clearly disclose material risks and document pre-treatment screening for arterial susceptibility factors. The decision suggests courts may weigh clinical opinion heavily over population-level evidence when assessing causation.
papers.key_finding: The trial court found the chiropractor liable for inadequate informed consent disclosure of material risks and implicitly attributed causation to manipulation, though the court acknowledged scientific probability of causation remained uncertain and did not fully consider interaction models (latent susceptibility plus trigger mechanism).
papers.study_design: Legal case analysis with clinical review

papers.title: Spinal Manipulative Therapy on a Healthy Population: Protocol for a Randomized Blinding Feasibility Trial
papers.one_line: Feasibility study validating a novel sham chiropractic manipulation to enable blinded clinical trials.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This research addresses a critical gap in chiropractic methodology by developing and testing a validated sham manipulation protocol. Successfully blinding participants is essential for rigorous clinical trials evaluating SMT efficacy. Chiropractors should monitor this trial's results as it may strengthen the evidence base for future chiropractic research and practice validation.
papers.key_finding: This is a protocol paper (ongoing trial with 18/60 participants enrolled as of December 2025). Primary outcome is blinding integrity using Bang Blinding Index; secondary outcomes assess gait parameters and James Blinding Index comparison between genuine and sham HVLA SMT.

papers.title: The 2023 patient profile and clinical management characteristics at a South African chiropractic training clinic: a descriptive cross-sectional study
papers.one_line: Describes patient demographics and management patterns at South African chiropractic teaching clinic.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This study documents real-world patient characteristics and treatment approaches in a chiropractic training setting, providing insight into case mix and management strategies. Chiropractors can benchmark their patient populations and clinical practices against a South African academic institution's experience.
papers.key_finding: The study profiles patient demographics and clinical management characteristics at a South African chiropractic training clinic in 2023, though specific findings cannot be determined without the abstract.

papers.title: Rehabilitation effects of combined respiratory guidance and chiropractic adjustment on adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis
papers.one_line: Combined respiratory guidance and chiropractic adjustment superior to conventional treatment for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Adding respiratory guidance to chiropractic adjustment for adolescent scoliosis patients yields significantly better outcomes in pain reduction, trunk symmetry, Cobb angle improvement, and quality of life compared to adjustment alone. Consider incorporating coordinated breathing techniques into spinal manipulation protocols for AIS patients to enhance muscle strength, flexibility, and functional capacity.
papers.key_finding: The combined respiratory guidance and chiropractic adjustment group achieved 96.72% treatment efficacy compared to 80.85% in the conventional group (P=0.017), with superior improvements in Cobb angle, trunk symmetry, back muscle strength, pain scores, and quality of life measures.

papers.title: Nationwide Online Stress Survey of 100,000 People in Japan
papers.one_line: High-stress individuals seek chiropractic massage as primary stress coping strategy.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize their role in stress management, particularly for male patients experiencing high stress. Consider incorporating stress assessment and patient education about sleep, work-life balance, and financial planning into practice, as these factors significantly influence stress levels. Market chiropractic services as a validated stress-reduction intervention.
papers.key_finding: Among high-stress individuals, men most commonly used chiropractic massage as a coping strategy, while women preferred bathroom time. Sleep duration, work hours, and household income were significant predictors of high-stress group membership.

papers.title: Recruiting US veterans with chronic low back pain in a multisite randomized pragmatic trial.
papers.one_line: Existing referrals most efficiently recruited VA veterans with chronic low back pain for chiropractic trial.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors in VA settings should leverage existing referral pathways and email communications for efficient patient recruitment, as these strategies reduced time-to-enrollment to 16-23 days. Combining recruitment methods—particularly EHR prescreening for female patients and referral-based approaches for racial/ethnic minorities—improves both enrollment speed and demographic diversity. Virtual baseline visits and email invitations significantly improved engagement compared to postal-only recruitment.
papers.key_finding: Existing chiropractic referrals recruited 91% of screened veterans with median 23-day enrollment; email invitations reduced response time to 16 days versus 30 days for postal-only; EHR prescreen yielded highest female representation (79%) while referrals best captured racial/ethnic minorities (33%).
papers.study_design: Pragmatic randomized controlled trial with recruitment strategy comparison

papers.title: Association of Chiropractic Colleges Educational Conference and Research Agenda Conference 2026: Connected Care
papers.one_line: Professional conference proceedings addressing connected care in chiropractic education and research.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This conference proceedings document provides access to peer-reviewed abstracts and research presentations focused on integrated, connected care models within chiropractic practice and education. Clinicians should review the platform and poster presentations to identify evidence-based approaches for enhancing interprofessional collaboration and patient care coordination.
papers.key_finding: The conference brought together chiropractic educators and researchers to present and discuss connected care initiatives across multiple platform and poster presentations, advancing the research agenda for the profession.

papers.title: Chiropractor perspectives on the use of patient reported outcome measures: a survey of Veterans Health Administration chiropractors.
papers.one_line: VHA chiropractors report varied adoption and perspectives on patient-reported outcome measures.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors in the VHA system recognize the importance of patient-reported outcomes for measuring treatment effectiveness, but implementation may vary significantly across clinics. Understanding barriers and facilitators to PROM adoption can improve clinical documentation and outcomes tracking in chiropractic care.
papers.key_finding: The survey identifies chiropractors' perspectives on integrating patient-reported outcome measures into Veterans Health Administration clinical practice, revealing insights into current usage patterns and perceived utility.

papers.title: Adverse events among older adults receiving chiropractic spinal manipulation and related treatments: an updated systematic review.
papers.one_line: Systematic review of adverse events from spinal manipulation in older adult populations.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This systematic review synthesizes safety data on spinal manipulation in older adults—a population at higher risk for complications. Chiropractors should review identified adverse events and apply appropriate risk stratification when treating elderly patients, particularly those with comorbidities or on medications affecting bone/vascular health.
papers.key_finding: The review examines the incidence and nature of adverse events associated with chiropractic spinal manipulation and related treatments specifically in older adult populations, providing updated evidence on safety outcomes.

papers.title: Musculoskeletal Treatments: Physical Modalities.
papers.one_line: Exercise-based therapies show moderate evidence; multimodal treatment approaches most effective for chronic musculoskeletal pain.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Incorporate exercise-based interventions as a cornerstone of chronic musculoskeletal pain management, supported by moderate-certainty evidence. Consider combining multiple treatment modalities (manual therapy, exercise, adjunctive therapies) within a structured rehabilitation framework rather than using isolated interventions. Manual therapies including spinal manipulative therapy have low-to-moderate evidence support across multiple body regions.
papers.key_finding: Chronic musculoskeletal pain disorders represent 70-80% of chronic pain diagnoses in the U.S. Multidisciplinary rehabilitation combining multiple modalities shows better outcomes than isolated treatments; exercise has moderate-certainty evidence, while manual therapies have lower certainty but remain relevant options.

papers.title: Women's health and chiropractic: Educational audit and development of core competencies.
papers.one_line: Developed 62 core competencies across 10 domains for women's health chiropractic education.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should be aware that evidence-based core competencies for women's health care now exist, covering lifespan considerations beyond reproductive health, including social determinants. Practices can use these 10 domains to self-assess their readiness to provide comprehensive women's health care and identify continuing education gaps. Educational institutions can implement these competencies to better prepare practitioners for evidence-informed management of female patients across all ages.
papers.key_finding: An international consensus panel of 42 experts approved 62 core competencies organized into 10 domains for women's health chiropractic practice, encompassing lifespan care, reproductive health, and social determinants of health in one round of Delphi review.
papers.study_design: Educational audit with Delphi consensus methodology

papers.title: The assessment of second year chiropractic students' comfort and confidence modifying care for vulnerable patient groups: A cross-sectional survey.
papers.one_line: Chiropractic students show lower confidence modifying care for physically disabled patients versus sociocultural vulnerable groups.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractic education should prioritize training in care modification for physically and mentally disabled patients, where student confidence gaps are largest. Educators should leverage students' existing comfort with diverse populations while addressing specific deficits in managing complex physical and mental health conditions. Consider pairing students with lived experience of disabilities (37% identified with special populations) as peer educators to improve clinical readiness.
papers.key_finding: Students demonstrated significantly lower comfort and confidence modifying care for physically and mentally disabled patients compared to general patient populations and sociocultural vulnerable groups. Notably, comfort levels exceeded confidence levels, suggesting students may overestimate their preparedness for complex patient modifications.

papers.title: A Mindbody Approach to Long-standing Fatigue: A Case Report on Emotional Somatic Release Using HeartSpeak Lite for BodyWork
papers.one_line: HeartSpeak Lite bodywork combining fascial mobilization with emotional processing improved chronic fatigue symptoms.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This case suggests integrating emotional somatic processing with manual therapy may benefit patients with treatment-resistant fatigue. The patient showed meaningful improvements in fatigue severity and stress over 10 sessions, suggesting a mindbody approach could complement traditional chiropractic care. Chiropractors may consider trauma-informed emotional awareness techniques alongside manual therapy for complex fatigue cases.
papers.key_finding: A 52-year-old with decade-long fatigue showed substantial improvement after 10 weeks of HeartSpeak Lite bodywork: Fatigue Severity Scale decreased from 6.8 to 4.2 and Perceived Stress Scale improved from 29 to 19, with reported increases in energy and physical activity tolerance.

papers.title: Adding Self-Care Complementary and Integrative Health (CIH) Therapies to Care for Chronic Pain—The APPROACH Study
papers.one_line: Combined practitioner and self-care CIH therapies equal practitioner-only care for chronic pain reduction.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Both practitioner-delivered CIH alone and combined with self-care (yoga, mindfulness, Tai Chi) produce equivalent functional improvements in chronic pain. However, adding self-care CIH therapies leads to greater perceived improvements in pain, fatigue, mental health, and overall well-being, suggesting value in comprehensive patient education about self-care options alongside chiropractic care.
papers.key_finding: Pain interference improved similarly in both groups (-0.62 vs -0.70), with ~40% achieving clinically meaningful improvement. The combined PD/SC-CIH arm showed superior patient-reported benefits across multiple domains including pain perception, fatigue, mental health, and well-being.

papers.title: Efficacy of manual therapy by different healthcare professionals on pain and function in temporomandibular disorders: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials
papers.one_line: Manual therapy reduces TMD pain and improves mouth opening short-term across professions.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Manual therapy shows promise for short-term pain relief and improved mouth opening in TMD patients, with physiotherapists demonstrating the most consistent outcomes in structured settings. Chiropractors should consider multiprofessional collaboration and recognize that current evidence supports short-term benefits; long-term effectiveness remains unclear and requires further investigation. Technique standardization and outcome tracking across practices could strengthen the evidence base for manual TMD management.
papers.key_finding: Manual therapy produced short-term reductions in pain and improvements in maximum mouth opening across different healthcare professionals, though evidence certainty was limited. Physiotherapists in rehabilitation settings demonstrated the most consistent results, while long-term effectiveness and superiority of specific approaches could not be firmly established.
papers.study_design: Systematic review of randomized controlled trials

papers.title: Physiological changes of cortisol and oxytocin following manual therapy: a scoping review
papers.one_line: Manual therapy produces variable cortisol and oxytocin responses; standardization needed.
papers.clinical_takeaway: While manual therapy may modulate stress hormones (cortisol) and bonding hormones (oxytocin), current evidence is inconsistent due to methodological variations across studies. Clinicians should recognize that neuroendocrine mechanisms are plausible but not yet definitively established. Future research with standardized protocols is needed to clarify whether hormonal changes are primary mechanisms or merely correlates of MT benefit.
papers.key_finding: Of 2,374 studies screened, 72 met criteria; studies showed mixed and variable cortisol and oxytocin responses to manual therapy across different MT types, populations, and measurement methods, with fewer studies examining oxytocin than cortisol.

papers.title: Spinal manipulative therapy promotes nucleus pulposus resorption and alleviates pain in a rat model of lumbar disc herniation via JNK-dependent regulation of inflammation and tissue remodeling
papers.one_line: SMT accelerates disc herniation resorption and pain relief through JNK-mediated inflammatory and tissue remodeling pathways.
papers.clinical_takeaway: SMT may promote endogenous healing of lumbar disc herniation by optimizing the inflammatory response rather than suppressing it, potentially offering superior outcomes compared to anti-inflammatory approaches. This mechanistic evidence supports SMT's clinical use for herniated disc pain, particularly for spontaneous resolution cases. Consider SMT as a primary intervention option before or alongside other treatments for acute LDH.
papers.key_finding: SMT significantly reduced mechanical allodynia from day 3 onward and achieved near-complete nucleus pulposus resorption by day 28, outperforming epidural corticosteroids. The therapeutic effects were entirely JNK-pathway dependent, as confirmed by complete abolishment of benefits in JNK-knockout mice.

papers.title: Effects of Spinal Manipulation and Dry Needling on Headache and Migraine: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials
papers.one_line: Systematic review evaluates spinal manipulation and dry needling efficacy for headache and migraine management.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This systematic review of RCTs provides evidence on the effectiveness of spinal manipulation and dry needling as treatment options for headache and migraine disorders. Chiropractors can reference this review to support clinical decision-making and patient education regarding these common interventions for headache management.
papers.key_finding: The review synthesizes RCT evidence on spinal manipulation and dry needling for headache and migraine conditions, offering a comprehensive assessment of their comparative effectiveness.
papers.study_design: Systematic review of randomized controlled trials

papers.title: One Spinal Manipulation Session Does Not Affect Static, Quasi-Static and Dynamic Balance or Pressure Pain Threshold in Individuals With Chronic Low Back Pain: A Randomized Clinical Controlled Trial
papers.one_line: Single spinal manipulation session produces no measurable changes in balance or pain sensitivity in chronic low back pain.
papers.clinical_takeaway: A single manipulation session does not acutely improve balance measures (static, quasi-static, or dynamic) or pressure pain thresholds in chronic low back pain patients. Clinicians should not expect immediate balance improvements from isolated manipulation and may need to consider multimodal or repeated treatment approaches for functional gains in this population.
papers.key_finding: Single spinal manipulation produced no statistically significant changes in SOT, SEBT, or pain pressure threshold immediately, at 24 hours, or 1 week post-intervention compared to placebo.

papers.title: Neck proprioception and mobility improved after upper neck and spine treatment: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.one_line: Upper cervical manipulation improved neck proprioception and mobility versus control.
papers.clinical_takeaway: The One-to-Zero system targeting the C0-C1 joint complex demonstrated superior improvements in cervical kinesthesia and range of motion compared to no treatment, suggesting upper cervical manipulation may normalize proprioceptive feedback. Clinicians may consider prioritizing upper cervical treatment when addressing neck dysfunction associated with proprioceptive deficits.
papers.key_finding: Treatment group showed significant improvements in head-to-target repositioning accuracy at 50% maximum rotation and greater variable error reduction in head-to-neutral tests, alongside improvements in ROM, pain, and neck disability compared to controls.

papers.title: Verbal framing, rather than measured cognitive-affective variables, is associated with short-term outcomes after spinal manipulation: a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial
papers.one_line: Verbal framing predicts short-term pain outcomes after spinal manipulation more than patient expectations.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Pre-treatment communication framing significantly influences immediate pain responses to spinal manipulation in young adults with chronic low back pain. Practitioners should focus on optimizing verbal framing before manipulation, as patient expectations and attitudes showed minimal independent association with short-term outcomes. Consider positive framing as a low-cost intervention to potentially enhance treatment response.
papers.key_finding: Verbal framing (positive, neutral, or negative) delivered before spinal manipulation was associated with short-term pain and pressure pain threshold changes, while pre-treatment expectations, attitudes toward manual therapy, and expectation fulfillment showed sparse and inconsistent associations with outcomes.
papers.study_design: Secondary analysis of randomized controlled trial

papers.title: Clinical features of manual therapy interventions in people with tension-type headache: A scoping review.
papers.one_line: Manual therapy for tension-type headache lacks standardization in technique, dosage, and mechanistic rationale.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Manual therapy shows promise for tension-type headache management, but current evidence lacks consistent protocols and clear mechanistic understanding. Chiropractors should standardize their approach by targeting cervical/suboccipital structures with defined treatment frequency/duration and document outcomes consistently. Future practice should be informed by mechanism-based reasoning rather than variable ad-hoc techniques.
papers.key_finding: 33 RCTs identified with wide variation in manual therapy techniques (manipulation, myofascial release, suboccipital inhibition, friction massage), treatment dosage, target structures, and outcome measures, limiting evidence synthesis and clinical interpretation.

papers.title: The Effect of Joint Mobilization and Manipulation on Proprioception: Systematic Review with Limited Meta-Analysis
papers.one_line: Joint mobilization and manipulation may improve proprioception through mechanoreceptor stimulation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Consider joint mobilization and manipulation as adjuncts to enhance proprioceptive function in patients with proprioceptive deficits. The evidence suggests these techniques activate mechanoreceptors, potentially improving joint position sense and neuromuscular control. Further high-quality trials are needed to establish optimal protocols and patient populations.
papers.key_finding: Joint mobilization and manipulation demonstrate potential to enhance proprioceptive function, likely through stimulation of joint mechanoreceptors and afferent nervous system feedback.

papers.title: Chiropractic Management of Adults with Cervicogenic or Tension-Type Headaches: Development of a Clinical Practice Guideline
papers.one_line: Evidence-based guideline supports spinal manipulation for cervicogenic headache and multimodal care for tension-type headache.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors can confidently use spinal manipulation as a primary intervention for cervicogenic headache based on moderate evidence. For tension-type headache, spinal manipulation should be combined with other modalities rather than used alone. Practitioners should incorporate red flag screening and proper examination protocols, while recognizing that acupuncture, meditation, and education lack sufficient evidence for standalone use.
papers.key_finding: Spinal manipulation is supported for cervicogenic headache management, while tension-type headache requires multimodal approaches. Evidence remains insufficient for strong recommendations regarding acupuncture, education, mindfulness, and isolated modalities.
papers.study_design: Umbrella review with Delphi consensus panel and clinical practice guideline development

papers.title: Effects of segmental spinal manipulation on adolescent scoliosis based on electromyography parameters
papers.one_line: Segmental spinal manipulation reduces Cobb angle and alters EMG recruitment patterns in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Segmental spinal manipulation may help correct spinal alignment in adolescent scoliosis patients by reducing Cobb angle measurements. However, the procedure appears to modulate muscle recruitment patterns rather than increase paraspinal muscle strength, suggesting its benefit is primarily biomechanical realignment rather than muscular strengthening.
papers.key_finding: Segmental spinal manipulation significantly increased EMG Turns (motor unit recruitment) in multiple positions and reduced Cobb angle compared to ordinary massage, though it did not demonstrate increased paraspinal muscle amplitude/strength.

papers.title: Mechano responsiveness of neuroimmune cross-talk in bone and joints: A narrative review with implications for force-based manipulations.
papers.one_line: Neuroimmune system mediates bone health; force-based manipulations may modulate these responses.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Spinal manipulation and manual therapy may influence bone-related neuroimmune responses, though direct evidence is limited. Chiropractors should individualize treatment considering patient age, hormonal status, and comorbidities, as these factors significantly affect neuroimmune-mediated bone health. Combining manual therapy with targeted physical activity may optimize therapeutic outcomes.
papers.key_finding: While substantial evidence supports physical activity's effects on bone neuroimmune responses, force-based manipulations (including spinal manipulation) show early promise for neuroimmune modulation despite limited direct evidence of bone changes. The neuroimmune system functions as a nonlinear network where nervous, immune, and endocrine systems reciprocally regulate bone cell function.

papers.title: Complications of Chiropractic Manipulation in a Patient With Von Willebrand Disease: A Clinical Case Report and Literature Review
papers.one_line: Chiropractic manipulation caused life-threatening iliopsoas hematoma in patient with Von Willebrand disease.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors must screen patients for bleeding disorders before manipulation, as spinal manipulation poses serious hemorrhagic risks in coagulopathic patients. Von Willebrand disease and other inherited bleeding disorders are relative contraindications to chiropractic manipulation. Referral to appropriate specialists and informed consent discussing bleeding risks are essential when patients have known or suspected coagulopathies.
papers.key_finding: A 32-year-old female with Von Willebrand disease developed an 896 cc iliopsoas hematoma with femoral nerve compression following routine chiropractic spinal manipulation, resulting in persistent neurological deficits despite intervention.

papers.title: Brain functional changes following spinal manipulation therapy in patients with lumbar disc herniation and chronic low back pain: a scoping review
papers.one_line: Spinal manipulation modulates brain networks, reducing pain and disability in lumbar disc herniation patients.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Spinal manipulation therapy produces measurable neuroplastic changes in the prefrontal cortex, default mode network, and visual network that correlate with pain reduction and improved function in chronic low back pain patients with disc herniation. These findings support a neurobiological mechanism for manipulation efficacy beyond mechanical correction alone. Chiropractors can reference these central nervous system changes when counseling patients about treatment expectations and outcomes.
papers.key_finding: Ten studies showed spinal manipulation induces significant brain activity and connectivity changes, particularly in prefrontal cortex and default mode network, correlating with improvements in pain intensity (VAS), functional disability (ODI, JOA), and mood disorders.

papers.title: Immediate effects of upper cervical spinal manipulation on cervical sensorimotor control in individuals with chronic primary cervical pain: an exploratory randomized controlled trial
papers.one_line: UCSM may transiently slow head-neck movement in cervical pain patients, suggesting accuracy-focused compensation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Upper cervical manipulation at C1-C2 appears to produce immediate kinematic changes in cervical pain patients, with movement slowing that may reflect a speed-accuracy trade-off. While sensorimotor control changes were observed, the clinical significance remains unclear pending larger, longer-term studies. These exploratory findings warrant cautious interpretation until validation in larger samples.
papers.key_finding: UCSM elicited transient slowing of head and neck movement on the cervical movement sense test compared to sham manipulation, potentially reflecting compensatory sensorimotor control or a speed-accuracy trade-off favoring accuracy.
papers.study_design: Exploratory randomized controlled trial, single-blind, sham-controlled

papers.title: The effect of Traditional Chinese Medicine Tuina massage combined with family-based prevention on visual acuity in children and adolescents with myopia: A case report of single-group interventional study
papers.one_line: TCM Tuina massage combined with blue-light glasses improved visual acuity in myopic children over 12 weeks.
papers.clinical_takeaway: TCM Tuina massage (3×/week) combined with blue-light-blocking glasses showed significant visual acuity improvements in pediatric myopia patients. Non-amblyopic children responded better than amblyopic cases. Lutein supplementation alone did not produce significant gains, suggesting the primary benefit derives from Tuina massage and behavioral interventions.
papers.key_finding: All participants demonstrated statistically significant visual acuity improvements post-intervention, with the blue-light-blocking glasses subgroup showing the most pronounced gains and non-amblyopic patients improving more than amblyopic patients.

papers.title: Spinal manipulative therapy for adults with chronic low back pain
papers.one_line: SMT shows small to medium benefits over sham/no treatment but similar effects to other conservative interventions for chronic LBP.
papers.clinical_takeaway: SMT may provide modest pain reduction and functional improvements compared to placebo or no treatment in chronic LBP patients. However, evidence quality is low-to-very-low, and SMT performs similarly to other conservative treatments, suggesting it should be considered one option among multiple evidence-based interventions rather than a first-line exclusive therapy.
papers.key_finding: SMT versus sham showed small pain reduction (MD -7.01 on 100-point scale) and medium functional improvement; versus no treatment showed medium pain improvement and large functional improvement; versus other conservative interventions showed little pain difference but small functional improvement. All evidence rated low-to-very-low certainty due to inconsistency and study limitations.
papers.study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials

papers.title: Non-Pharmacological and Pharmacological Treatments for Non-Acute Lumbar Disc Herniation: A Protocol for a Multicenter Pragmatic Trial
papers.one_line: Pragmatic RCT protocol comparing acupuncture/spinal manipulation versus pharmacological treatment for non-acute lumbar disc herniation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This upcoming multicenter trial will provide high-quality evidence on the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of non-pharmacological strategies (acupuncture and spinal manipulation) versus pharmacological interventions for non-acute LDH over 3 years. Chiropractors can anticipate robust comparative data on manual therapy efficacy, which may support evidence-based treatment decision-making for disc herniation patients. Results expected to inform optimal management strategies and relative value of manual therapies versus pharmaceutical approaches.
papers.key_finding: Protocol study—no results yet. Designed to compare effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, and safety of non-pharmacological treatment (acupuncture and spinal manipulation) versus pharmacological interventions for non-acute LDH, with primary outcomes measured at 13 weeks using Oswestry Disability Index and Numerical Rating Scale.
papers.study_design: Multicenter pragmatic randomized controlled trial (RCT protocol)

papers.title: Response to Letter to the Editor regarding "Can pre-treatment verbal suggestions influence the short-term effects of spinal manipulation in young adults with chronic non-specific low back pain? A randomized controlled trial"
papers.one_line: Authors respond to editorial critique on verbal suggestion effects during spinal manipulation for low back pain.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This response addresses methodological questions about how practitioner communication and expectation-setting may modulate spinal manipulation outcomes. Clinicians should consider that verbal framing before treatment may influence patient perception of treatment efficacy.
papers.key_finding: Authors defend their RCT methodology examining whether pre-treatment verbal suggestions enhance short-term effects of spinal manipulation in chronic non-specific low back pain patients.

papers.title: Angular Kinematic Analysis of Supine Cervical Thrusts Performed by Chiropractors and Chiropractic Students on Mannequins
papers.one_line: Expert chiropractors produce peak cervical rotation of 34° with 193°/s velocity during manipulation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Experienced DCs achieve consistent cervical rotation patterns (19.3° onset, 33.9° peak) with measurable kinematic parameters that could serve as performance benchmarks. These data provide objective reference values for teaching cervical thrust technique and evaluating student progression toward expert-level manipulation characteristics.
papers.key_finding: Doctors of chiropractic produced mean peak axial rotation of 33.9° at thrust peak, with 14.6° rotation occurring in 144 milliseconds at maximum rotational velocity of 192.9°/s and acceleration of 4427°/s².

papers.title: Kinematic Assessment of Hip, Shoulder, and Elbow Movements of a Chiropractor Performing Side Posture Adjustments: Results From a Biomechanical Analysis.
papers.one_line: Side-posture spinal manipulation involves consistent kinematic patterns emphasizing body drop over isolated upper extremity force.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Effective side-posture adjustments rely on coordinated hip, shoulder, and elbow positioning with emphasis on controlled body weight transfer rather than isolated arm force. Practitioners should focus on consistent setup angles and proper body mechanics, recognizing that individual variations in technique may reflect differences in training, table height, and patient factors. Understanding the biomechanical role of each joint—particularly limited elbow extension during thrust—can optimize force delivery and reduce practitioner injury risk.
papers.key_finding: Side-posture adjustments demonstrate repeatable kinematic patterns across multiple trials despite variable angular magnitudes, with thrust force primarily generated through hip and shoulder positioning (body drop) rather than elbow extension alone.

papers.title: CT-guided Foramen Ovale Injection of Mesenchymal Stem Cells: First Human Case Report of Trigeminal Neuralgia Relief
papers.one_line: MSC injection via foramen ovale provided sustained trigeminal neuralgia pain relief in one patient.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This case suggests MSC injection may offer an alternative for TN patients failing conservative care, though evidence remains limited to a single case. Chiropractors should be aware of this emerging intervention when referring refractory TN patients to interventional pain specialists. Long-term efficacy and safety require larger prospective trials before clinical adoption.
papers.key_finding: A 48-year-old woman with 22-year refractory trigeminal neuralgia experienced dramatic pain reduction and medication discontinuation at 1 month post-MSC injection, with sustained cognitive improvements at 12 months despite partial symptom recurrence.

papers.title: The effects of chiropractic adjustment on inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity in children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder: a pilot RCT
papers.one_line: Chiropractic adjustments showed no significant advantage over sham treatment for pediatric ADHD symptoms.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This pilot study found that while both chiropractic adjustment plus usual care and sham treatment plus usual care improved ADHD symptoms, there were no significant differences between groups, suggesting improvements were likely due to usual care rather than the adjustments themselves. Chiropractors should not promote spinal manipulation as a primary treatment for ADHD in children based on current evidence. Further rigorous research with larger samples is needed before drawing conclusions about chiropractic's role in ADHD management.
papers.key_finding: Both groups demonstrated significant improvements in ADHD symptoms over 8 weeks, but there were no statistically significant differences between chiropractic adjustment plus usual care and sham adjustment plus usual care groups.

papers.title: Myositis Ossificans Traumatica of Bilateral Sternocleidomastoid Muscles After Chiropractor Adjustment: A Case Report
papers.one_line: Chiropractic neck adjustment preceded myositis ossificans development in a post-surgical patient.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should exercise heightened caution with patients having recent neck surgery or tissue trauma, as mechanical manipulation may precipitate heterotopic ossification. Recognition of post-adjustment neck stiffness, trismus, and progressive pain warrants immediate medical referral to rule out serious complications like myositis ossificans.
papers.key_finding: A young woman developed bilateral sternocleidomastoid myositis ossificans following chiropractic neck adjustment, with imaging showing heterotopic ossification extending from the surgical site into adjacent musculature.

papers.title: Vertebral Subluxation and Systems Biology: An Integrative Review Exploring the Salutogenic Influence of Chiropractic Care on the Neuroendocrine-Immune System
papers.one_line: Chiropractic care may influence neuroendocrine-immune function through multiple neural pathways beyond musculoskeletal effects.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Consider documenting systemic health markers (blood pressure, heart rate variability, sleep quality) in patient records as potential salutogenic outcomes of chiropractic care. This integrative perspective supports discussing broader health benefits with patients while recognizing that precise neural mechanisms require further research. Use these findings to inform patient education about potential systemic effects beyond symptomatic relief.
papers.key_finding: Evidence suggests chiropractic adjustment may favorably influence neuroendocrine-immune system function and physical well-being markers (blood pressure, HRV, sleep) through neurologically mediated pathways, though specific mechanisms remain incompletely mapped.

papers.title: A Case Report of U-Type Sacral Fracture After Chiropractic Adjustment.
papers.one_line: Drop-table chiropractic manipulation caused severe U-type sacral fracture in elderly patient.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Drop-table manipulation poses serious risk of spinopelvic dissociation, particularly in older patients. Practitioners must exercise extreme caution with high-velocity techniques in this population and understand potential for severe bilateral sacral injury. Consider risk-benefit analysis and alternative approaches in elderly patients with suspected bone quality concerns.
papers.key_finding: A 74-year-old male sustained a U-type sacral fracture (spinopelvic dissociation) directly attributable to drop-table chiropractic manipulation, resulting in prolonged hospitalization and delayed diagnosis despite conservative management leading to functional recovery.

papers.title: Absence of Neuroplastic Changes in the Bilateral H-Reflex Amplitude following Spinal Manipulation with Activator IV.
papers.one_line: Activator IV spinal manipulation does not produce measurable changes in H-reflex amplitude.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Activator IV manipulation may not modulate spinal cord reflex excitability as measured by H-reflex testing. This suggests alternative mechanisms may explain clinical benefits if they occur. Consider that neurophysiological effects via H-reflex changes are not the primary mechanism for this manipulation technique.
papers.key_finding: Bilateral H-reflex amplitude showed no significant neuroplastic changes following Activator IV spinal manipulation, indicating this technique does not alter spinal cord reflex responsiveness.

papers.title: Acute Lumbar Schmorl's Node Following Chiropractic Adjustment
papers.one_line: Acute Schmorl's node developed post-chiropractic adjustment but resolved with conservative care.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should be aware that spinal manipulation can precipitate acute Schmorl's nodes, though they typically remain benign and responsive to conservative management. This case demonstrates that even when complications occur, patient outcomes can be favorable with appropriate conservative care protocols.
papers.key_finding: A 41-year-old male developed an acute Schmorl's node at L4-L5 immediately following chiropractic manipulation and achieved 85% pain relief with conservative treatment, suggesting these acute lesions are generally self-limiting.

papers.title: Management of people with low back pain: a survey of opinions and beliefs of Dutch and Belgian chiropractors.
papers.one_line: Dutch and Belgian chiropractors show 64.5% adherence to LBP clinical guidelines, with gaps in acute care and return-to-work advice.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should strengthen adherence to evidence-based guidelines, particularly for acute LBP management and return-to-work counseling. While most practitioners correctly advise against bedrest (98.5%), only 59.4% address return-to-work recommendations and 77.5% emphasize staying active. Practitioners are encouraged to supplement spinal adjustments with more consistent exercise prescription and functional advice.
papers.key_finding: Overall guideline adherence was 64.5%, with better performance in chronic cases (73.4%) versus acute cases (55.9%). Chiropractors showed strongest adherence to bedrest limitation (98.5%) but weakest performance on return-to-work guidance (59.4%).

papers.title: Chiropractic Spinal Manipulation Prevents Secondary Hyperalgesia Induced by Topical Capsaicin in Healthy Individuals
papers.one_line: Spinal manipulation may prevent capsaicin-induced secondary hyperalgesia in healthy subjects.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This research suggests spinal manipulation has analgesic properties that may modulate central pain processing mechanisms. The preventive effect on secondary hyperalgesia indicates potential neuroprotective applications, though clinical translation requires studies in symptomatic populations.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractic spinal manipulation prevented the development of secondary hyperalgesia when administered before topical capsaicin application, suggesting manipulation may alter central sensitization pathways.

papers.title: The prevalence of complementary and alternative medicine use among Turkish patients with primary headache.
papers.one_line: One-third of Turkish headache patients use CAM, with chiropractic adjustment among top modalities.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should recognize that 33% of primary headache patients in this Turkish population use CAM, with chiropractic adjustment being utilized by 17.5% of CAM users. Longer disease duration strongly predicts CAM use, suggesting patients with chronic headaches actively seek complementary treatments. Consider screening for concurrent CAM use and discussing evidence-based outcomes with headache patients.
papers.key_finding: CAM use was reported in 33.3% of primary headache patients, with phytotherapy (37.5%), cupping (27.5%), and chiropractic adjustment (17.5%) being most common. Longer disease duration was the only significant predictor of CAM use (p=0.002).

papers.title: Resolution of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease Following Correction for Upper Cross Syndrome-A Case Study and Brief Review
papers.one_line: Upper cross syndrome correction via chiropractic care resolved concurrent GERD symptoms in one patient.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Consider postural assessment and correction in patients presenting with GERD, as upper cross syndrome may be a contributing factor. Cervical adjustments combined with soft tissue therapy targeting postural dysfunction may provide symptomatic relief beyond typical musculoskeletal complaints. Long-term postural maintenance with regular adjustments appears beneficial for symptom prevention.
papers.key_finding: A 35-year-old female with upper cross syndrome and GERD experienced complete resolution of both neck/back pain and reflux symptoms following chiropractic treatment focused on postural correction, with sustained improvement at 12-month follow-up.

papers.title: Chiropractic Day: A Historical Review of a Day Worth Celebrating
papers.one_line: Historical overview of Chiropractic Day's significance since Palmer's first adjustment in 1895.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractic Day (September 18) commemorates the profession's founding and offers practitioners an opportunity to reflect on their role in patient care. Consider using this day to engage in community education, volunteer activities, and professional development to honor the profession's history and advance its mission.
papers.key_finding: September 18, 1895, marks D.D. Palmer's first chiropractic adjustment; the profession has celebrated this date through various names and activities for over 125 years to honor its origins and mission.

papers.title: The effect of sacroiliac chiropractic adjustments on innominate angles.
papers.one_line: Sacroiliac adjustments produce measurable changes in innominate bone angles toward neutral alignment.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors can objectively document SIJ adjustment effectiveness using palpation measurement tools, demonstrating biomechanical corrections in innominate angles. This provides quantifiable evidence of treatment-induced pelvic realignment to support clinical decision-making and patient communication about SIJ dysfunction management.
papers.key_finding: Specific chiropractic sacroiliac adjustments produced measurable changes in innominate bone angles, moving the pelvis toward neutral anatomical alignment, while sham ultrasound control showed no significant changes.

papers.title: Changes in radiographic parameters following chiropractic treatment in 10 patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: A retrospective chart review
papers.one_line: Chiropractic adjustment reduced Cobb angles by 21.2% in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis cases.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This small retrospective study suggests chiropractic care may reduce Cobb angles by ~6° and stabilize curves in adolescent scoliosis patients, particularly those with mild-to-moderate curves. However, the lack of control group, small sample size (n=10), and retrospective design limit generalizability; larger RCTs are needed before drawing clinical conclusions.
papers.key_finding: Mean Cobb angle decreased from 29.7° to 23.4° (21.2% reduction); 64% showed morphological improvement and 36% showed stabilization with no progression.

papers.title: Characterization of Horse Use in Therapeutic Horseback Riding Programs in the United States: A Pilot Survey
papers.one_line: Therapeutic horseback riding horses work moderately with lameness and back soreness as primary health issues.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors working with therapeutic riding programs should recognize that back soreness and lameness are the most common health concerns in these horses, with chiropractic adjustments being a frequently utilized complementary therapy. Understanding the workload (4 days/week, 2 hours/day) and typical horse demographics can inform appropriate care protocols and help establish evidence-based standards for equine wellness in THR settings.
papers.key_finding: Therapeutic horseback riding horses are worked below maximum PATH International recommendations (median 4 days/week, 2 hours/day), with back soreness and limb lameness as the most frequently reported health issues. Chiropractic adjustments and massage were among the most common complementary therapies utilized.

papers.title: Measurement and Analysis of Biomechanical Outcomes of Chiropractic Adjustment Performance in Chiropractic Education and Practice.
papers.one_line: Experienced chiropractors deliver McTimoney adjustments with significantly shorter thrust times than students.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Experienced practitioners achieve faster, more consistent thrust delivery with less variability—suggesting that practice and training optimize adjustment biomechanics. Monitoring thrust timing and consistency may serve as useful performance feedback during chiropractic education and technique refinement. Dominant hand dominance in peak force delivery suggests laterality considerations in adjustment training.
papers.key_finding: Experienced chiropractors (DCs) delivered McTimoney toggle-torque-recoil thrusts approximately 3 times faster to peak force (70 ms vs. 230 ms) and 2.5 times faster overall (118 ms vs. 284 ms) than third-year students, with significantly less variability and reduced total thrust time (1.27 s vs. 1.89 s).

papers.title: Traumatic spinal injuries: A retrospective epidemiological analysis following the 2018 driving policy reform in Saudi Arabia.
papers.one_line: Traumatic spinal injuries predominantly affect young males; lumbar injuries dominate with favorable neurological outcomes.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Most traumatic spinal injuries (93.7%) present without neurological deficits, primarily affecting the lumbar spine. Female patients and those with psychiatric history require extended care coordination. Cervical injuries and vertebral subluxation/dislocation carry higher neurological severity and warrant careful assessment and possible surgical consideration.
papers.key_finding: Motor vehicle accidents account for 57.6% of traumatic spinal injuries with a 3.7:1 male-to-female ratio; 93.7% of patients remained neurologically intact (AIS E). Longer hospital stays associated with psychiatric history, higher AIS severity, pulmonary infection, and ICU admission.

papers.title: Management of Cervical lateral mass fractures - A systematic review
papers.one_line: Floating lateral mass fractures require surgical intervention due to inherent spinal instability.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Floating lateral mass fractures (FLM) of the cervical spine are rare but serious injuries that cause spinal instability and frequently result in vertebral subluxation when treated conservatively (31% nonoperatively). Chiropractors should recognize FLM as a contraindication to manual therapy and refer these patients for surgical evaluation, as ACDF is the preferred treatment with minimal post-operative subluxation rates.
papers.key_finding: Among 332 FLM patients, 31% of those treated nonoperatively developed vertebral subluxation, while surgical management (primarily ACDF) resulted in minimal post-operative subluxation, establishing surgery as the preferred treatment modality.

papers.title: Animal Chiropractic: A Basic Description and Its Importance in Veterinary Practice.
papers.one_line: Animal chiropractic improves function and recovery in veterinary patients through neurological optimization.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Animal chiropractic is a safe, evidence-supported modality that should only be delivered by licensed professionals with postgraduate training. Incorporating animal chiropractic into veterinary practice can enhance patient conditioning, performance, and postoperative recovery by improving neurological input and motor output.
papers.key_finding: Properly applied animal chiropractic enhances patient strength, stability, and mobility by improving afferent input and modulating ventral horn motor neurons, thereby optimizing functional outcomes and recovery.

papers.title: Sublaminar stabilization (stapling) of the caudal cervical instability in Yorkshire terrier-A case report.
papers.one_line: Sublaminar stapling successfully stabilized cervical spine instability in a toy breed dog.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This case demonstrates that sublaminar stabilization via dorsal approach can be effective for cervical spine instability when conservative treatment fails. While this is veterinary orthopedic surgery, chiropractors should recognize that persistent neck pain and proprioceptive deficits refractory to conservative care warrant surgical referral to rule out structural instability.
papers.key_finding: A Yorkshire terrier with C6-C7 instability and tetraparesis unresponsive to 20 months of conservative treatment achieved ambulatory recovery and sustained neurological improvement five years after sublaminar stabilization surgery, despite requiring a revision procedure.

papers.title: Atlas Subluxation Complex, National Upper Cervical Chiropractic Association Intervention, and Dizziness Improvement: A Narrative Review of Historical Perspectives, Literature Synthesis, and a Path for Future Care
papers.one_line: Atlas subluxation may contribute to dizziness and be treatable with NUCCA chiropractic care.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Consider atlas subluxation as a potential etiological factor in patients presenting with dizziness, particularly when standard diagnostics are inconclusive. NUCCA technique may offer a therapeutic option for dizziness cases, though evidence remains preliminary and higher-quality research is needed to establish clinical efficacy and guide patient selection.
papers.key_finding: Conceptual evidence, case reports, and theoretical frameworks suggest atlas subluxation complex may contribute to dizziness pathogenesis and that NUCCA chiropractic intervention may improve dizziness outcomes, but high-quality RCTs are lacking.

papers.title: Catastrophic failure of anterior fusion for bilateral cervical facet dislocation: illustrative case
papers.one_line: Anterior-only fusion fails in bilateral cervical facet dislocation; combined anterior-posterior fixation recommended.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Bilateral cervical facet dislocations with posterior ligamentous complex damage, endplate/facet fractures, or pedicle involvement have high anterior fusion failure risk. Chiropractors should recognize these patients require surgical consultation and combined fixation approaches rather than anterior-only procedures. Awareness of these risk factors helps guide appropriate referral and prevents recurrent subluxation and spinal cord injury.
papers.key_finding: Anterior-alone fusion resulted in construct failure, recurrent vertebral subluxation, and spinal cord injury in a bilateral facet dislocation case. Risk factors include age, bilateral facet injury, extensive posterior ligamentous damage, and associated fractures (endplate, facet, pedicle).

papers.title: The Dark Side of Musculoskeletal Care: Why Do Ineffective Techniques Seem to Work? A Comprehensive Review of Complementary and Alternative Therapies
papers.one_line: Chiropractic and osteopathy lack robust evidence; observed benefits may derive primarily from placebo effects.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This critical review questions the biological plausibility of foundational chiropractic concepts like vertebral subluxation and argues that many reported benefits reflect placebo rather than specific therapeutic mechanisms. Chiropractors should prioritize evidence-based interventions, acknowledge placebo contributions to outcomes, and engage patients transparently about mechanism of action limitations to maintain ethical practice.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractic and osteopathic theories lack robust empirical validation; observed clinical benefits appear largely mediated by placebo responses and contextual/psychosocial factors rather than specific biological mechanisms.

papers.title: Vertebral Column Subluxation in Neurofibromatosis Type 1-Associated Dystrophic Scoliosis: A Report of Two Cases and Narrative Review
papers.one_line: Vertebral subluxation in NF1-associated dystrophic scoliosis requires surgical intervention; halo-gravity traction carries significant complications.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors encountering patients with NF1-associated dystrophic scoliosis should recognize that vertebral subluxation is a serious complication requiring surgical referral. Conservative bracing management is frequently unsuccessful in NF1 scoliosis, and manipulation or traction is contraindicated due to risk of spinal cord injury and vascular compromise. Early recognition of progressive deformity and prompt surgical consultation are critical for patient safety.
papers.key_finding: Two cases of vertebral subluxation in NF1-associated dystrophic scoliosis were managed surgically with partial vertebral column resection; halo-gravity traction proved ineffective and caused serious vascular and neurological complications in one patient.
papers.study_design: Case report with narrative literature review

papers.title: The best preferable sagittal vertical axis for the ankylosis spondylitis with thoracolumbar kyphosis following one-level pedicle subtraction osteotomy under different cervical range of motion
papers.one_line: Optimal sagittal vertical axis alignment varies with cervical mobility in ankylosing spondylitis kyphosis correction.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Pedicle subtraction osteotomy outcomes in ankylosing spondylitis depend on individualizing sagittal vertical axis targets based on patient cervical range of motion. Chiropractors managing AS kyphosis should coordinate with surgical specialists to understand these biomechanical considerations for post-operative rehabilitation.
papers.key_finding: One-level pedicle subtraction osteotomy for ankylosing spondylitis thoracolumbar kyphosis requires personalized sagittal vertical axis alignment targets that account for cervical spine mobility to optimize postoperative outcomes.

papers.title: Secondary Analysis of a Dataset to Estimate the Prevalence of Vertebral Subluxation and Its Implications for Health Promotion and Prevention
papers.one_line: Vertebral subluxation identified in 78.6% of chiropractic patients using operational definition.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This retrospective analysis found high prevalence of vertebral subluxation (78.55%) across diverse patient presentations at multiple clinics, supporting a potential preventative health role for chiropractic care. However, the nonrandom sampling (only chiropractic clinic patients) limits generalizability; results reflect those already seeking chiropractic care rather than population-wide prevalence. Use findings to support patient education about spinal health and wellness positioning.
papers.key_finding: Among 1,851 chiropractic patients across 7 clinics in 4 states, 78.55% met the operational definition of vertebral subluxation, with prevalence ≥50% across all age and gender subgroups.
papers.study_design: Secondary analysis, retrospective quantitative cohort study

papers.title: Associations between demographics and clinical ideology, beliefs, and practice patterns: a secondary analysis of a survey of randomly sampled United States chiropractors.
papers.one_line: US chiropractor ideology and practices vary significantly by education program, experience, and geography.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should be aware that their peers hold diverse and sometimes conflicting beliefs about subluxation, vaccination, cancer treatment, and x-ray use depending on training background and location. This professional heterogeneity may affect public trust and interprofessional relationships; practitioners should consider evidence-based alignment on core clinical practices. Understanding these variations can help individual chiropractors reflect on their own ideology and ensure their messaging aligns with current best evidence.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractic degree program of graduation, years in practice, and geographic region are significantly associated with variation in clinical ideology and practice patterns across seven key domains including subluxation detection, vaccination attitudes, and cancer treatment claims.

papers.title: Spinal decompression and stabilisation in a cat with lumbar vertebral pathological fracture and subluxation, following discospondylitis and spinal epidural empyema.
papers.one_line: Surgical decompression and stabilization successfully treated feline spinal infection with fracture-subluxation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: While this is a veterinary case, it demonstrates the critical importance of imaging (MRI/CT) and surgical intervention when progressive neurological deterioration occurs despite medical management of spinal infections. The case illustrates that pathological fractures with subluxation may require stabilization beyond medical therapy alone, a principle potentially applicable to severe human spinal infections.
papers.key_finding: A cat with discospondylitis, epidural empyema, and pathological L1-L2 fracture/subluxation progressed from paraparesis to paraplegia despite medical therapy, but achieved optimal outcome following hemilaminectomy, decompression, and surgical stabilization with polymethylmethacrylate fixation.

papers.title: Veterinary Spinal Manipulative Therapy or Animal Chiropractic in Veterinary Rehabilitation
papers.one_line: Animal chiropractic is a receptor-based modality with growing clinical application in veterinary rehabilitation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Animal chiropractic operates through receptor-based mechanisms affecting neuro-anatomical and biomechanical function. Veterinarians and animal chiropractors should understand indications, contraindications, and when additional diagnostics are warranted before treatment. This multimodal approach integrates with broader veterinary rehabilitation protocols.
papers.key_finding: Veterinary spinal manipulative therapy is increasingly used in rehabilitation settings with receptor-based mechanisms, but clinicians must recognize its limitations and when further diagnostic evaluation is necessary.

papers.title: A novel Hinge-Link correction system for vertebral column resection: a pilot study in a porcine model.
papers.one_line: Novel Hinge-Link system achieves 94% scoliosis correction in porcine VCR model with neurological safety.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This pilot study demonstrates a promising surgical technique for severe scoliosis correction using a novel fixation device that provides three-dimensional control and neurological safety. While this is preclinical research in animals, chiropractors should be aware of emerging surgical options for severe cases requiring surgical referral and understand the potential benefits of advanced correction systems.
papers.key_finding: The Hinge-Link system achieved 94% correction of surgically created thoracic scoliosis (from 32° to 1.8°) in all pigs with no neurological deficits, subluxation, or dural impingement.

papers.title: Remodeling morphology of the subluxated osteotomy vertebra in closing-opening wedge osteotomy in ankylosing spondylitis: would the anterior bony beak blunt?
papers.one_line: AS patients undergoing lumbar osteotomy show favorable bony remodeling but limited spinal canal adaptation with subluxation.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Closing-opening wedge osteotomy for AS-related thoracolumbar kyphosis produces favorable long-term bony remodeling with adaptive resorption of anterior bony beaks. However, vertebral subluxation (≥5mm translation) significantly impairs spinal canal remodeling and limits correction maintenance, suggesting careful patient selection and monitoring for subluxation risk.
papers.key_finding: After COWO in AS patients, new bone formation and adaptive resorption of anterior bony beaks occurred favorably during 2+ year follow-up; however, patients with vertebral subluxation showed significantly impaired spinal canal remodeling capacity and greater loss of global kyphosis correction.

papers.title: Use of computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging to assess a case of spinal injury in a Showa koi Cyprinus carpio
papers.one_line: CT and MRI identified spinal cord compression and myelomalacia in a koi fish with neurological symptoms.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This case demonstrates advanced imaging's role in diagnosing spinal pathology in non-mammalian vertebrates. While not directly applicable to human chiropractic, it illustrates how cross-sectional imaging can reveal spinal cord compression and tissue damage underlying neurological dysfunction. The principle of imaging-guided assessment of vertebral subluxations and spinal cord integrity may inform diagnostic approaches.
papers.key_finding: MRI revealed extensive vertebral centra alteration and multifocal spinal cord compression associated with vertebral subluxation and severe myelomalacia that correlated with the patient's neurological decline.

papers.title: Posterior 3-Column Osteotomy for Treatment of Congenital Kyphosis with Multiple Thoracolumbar/Lumbar Anterior Unsegmented Vertebrae: A Comparison Between Patients with Increasing Number of Anterior Unsegmented Vertebrae
papers.one_line: Single-level posterior osteotomy efficacy decreases with ≥4 anterior unsegmented vertebrae in congenital kyphosis.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors managing congenital kyphosis patients should recognize that surgical outcomes differ significantly based on the number of anterior unsegmented vertebrae, with ≥4 vertebrae associated with higher complication rates and lower correction rates. This distinction is important for appropriate referral timing and setting realistic patient expectations for surgical outcomes and post-operative management.
papers.key_finding: Patients with ≥4 anterior unsegmented vertebrae had significantly higher remaining kyphosis (33.6° vs. 15.1°), lower correction rates (61.2% vs. 75.0%), and higher complication rates (66.7% vs. 7.7%) compared to those with 3 anterior unsegmented vertebrae.

papers.title: Evaluation of United States chiropractic professional subgroups: a survey of randomly sampled chiropractors.
papers.one_line: US chiropractors stratify into three distinct subgroups with different clinical ideologies and practice approaches.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors can expect significant practice philosophy diversity within the profession: 57% spine/neuromusculoskeletal focused, 22% primary care focused, and 21% vertebral subluxation focused. Understanding these subgroups helps practitioners recognize where they fit professionally and facilitates more targeted interdisciplinary collaboration. This segmentation reflects real differences in clinical beliefs and practice behaviors that should inform how chiropractors communicate their scope to other healthcare providers.
papers.key_finding: Three distinct professional subgroups self-identified based on perceived role in healthcare: spine/neuromusculoskeletal (56.8%), primary care (22.0%), and vertebral subluxation (21.2%) focused practitioners, each with substantially different clinical ideology and practice characteristics.

papers.title: The association between chiropractors' view of practice and patient encounter-level characteristics in Ontario, Canada: a cross-sectional study
papers.one_line: Chiropractors with unorthodox views treat more non-musculoskeletal conditions and diagnose subluxation more frequently.
papers.clinical_takeaway: Chiropractors should be aware that philosophical views about vertebral subluxation significantly influence practice patterns, particularly the types of conditions treated and diagnostic approaches used. Understanding these differences is important for interprofessional collaboration and managing patient expectations about evidence-based care versus condition-specific musculoskeletal treatment.
papers.key_finding: Chiropractors holding unorthodox views (vertebral subluxation affects overall health) had 16.5 times higher odds of treating non-musculoskeletal conditions and 63 times higher odds of diagnosing subluxation compared to orthodox practitioners. Encounters were shorter (0.6x duration) for unorthodox practitioners.

papers.title: Chiropractic Research Digest - 6 Months ending April 05, 2026
papers.one_line: No papers reviewed in this digest period.
papers.clinical_takeaway: This digest contains no reviewed papers and therefore provides no clinical recommendations or evidence for chiropractors to implement. Practitioners should consult other current research sources for evidence-based updates.
papers.key_finding: This appears to be an automatically generated digest template with zero papers reviewed during the 6-month period.
